text:
ci-bot: :rotating_light: Canary failing for rollout r-2026-03-15-42, health check flap on service inference-frontend. 5/5 canaries unhealthy in eu-west-1. Image tag: prod-canary -> digest sha256:abcd1234

incident-bot: Paging oncall team: @maya (oncall) — incident severity S2 (canary failures during deploy). Please acknowledge.

maya: ack. I’m booting into zoom and looking at the canary cluster now.

jon: seen similar errors on staging yesterday when we had a bad image tag. stack traces show mismatch: container expecting libcuda.so. We might have the wrong base image.

ashley: I'm looking at the CI artifact registry. There are two tags: `prod-canary` and `prod-canary-latest`. The digest in the canary rollout (abcd1234) matches an older release (r-2026-03-08) — hmm.

leo: suspect: our pipeline's `tag` step might have used a cached tag on the build node. We've seen cache poisoning before when the build cache isn't fully flushed after a force-rebuild.

maya: immediate action: kill-switch the canary feature flag and stop further canary traffic. @ops-oncall can you pause the rollout in the controller?

ops-oncall: pausing rollout now. `kubectl rollout pause deployment/inference-frontend -n eu-west-1` done. No new pods will be created.

jon: to be safe, flip kill-switch for canary routing: `POST /admin/flags/canary-route {enabled:false}` (internal). I’ll run that now.

jon: flipped. Confirmed 0% traffic to canaries.

incident-bot: Note: rollback recommended when canaries show config or artifact mismatch.

maya: we need to determine customer impact. Any errors reaching production? telemetry shows 0.6% increased 5xxs in eu-west-1 during the 3m window, but fronting load-balancer handled failover. No customer-facing incident reported yet.

ashley: pulling registry metadata:
```
# curl -s https://registry.internal/redwood/inference-frontend/tags | jq '.[] | select(.name=="prod-canary")'
{"name":"prod-canary","digest":"sha256:abcd1234","pushed_by":"ci-runner-12","created_at":"2026-03-08T02:14:00Z"}
```

ashley: latest build for r-2026-03-15 produced digest `sha256:efgh5678` but tag step appears to have attached `prod-canary-latest` to efgh5678 and mistakenly re-tagged the older digest as `prod-canary` due to a race in the tagging script when multiple runners share the ephemeral tag.

leo: root cause candidate: our tag reconciliation script uses a shared ephemeral lock file on NFS that doesn't atomic-lock across runners. If two builds run concurrently, the older digest can be re-tagged. This is classic cache/locking issue.

maya: mitigation plan: 1) Rollback canary tag to correct digest? 2) Promote correct digest to prod-canary after validation? 3) Fix pipeline to use immutable tags only (build-hash) and remove mutable shared tag.

jon: for immediate mitigation we should: A) Pin the canary deployment to digest `sha256:efgh5678` manually to test if that fixes the health check. B) If health checks pass, resume canary with the pinned digest.

ashley: pinning now. `kubectl set image deployment/inference-frontend inference-frontend=registry.internal/redwood/inference-frontend@sha256:efgh5678 -n eu-west-1 --record`

ops-oncall: new pods launching with efgh5678. Waiting for readiness probes.

maya: monitoring... 2/3 new pods ready, health check stabilized. Canaries now healthy for the pinned digest.

jon: good — that confirms the artifact mismatch. We should still roll back the bad tag mutation to avoid accidental auto-rollouts.

ashley: I've revoked the `prod-canary` mutable tag from registry and re-created it pointing to efgh5678. Also added temporary protected tag policy so only a single CI runner can update it.

leo: creating a ticket to rework tagging pipeline to always write immutable tags and a separate index for human-friendly names. Will include test for concurrent runs. PR reference: https://git.internal/redwood/infra-ci/pulls/412

maya: summary so far: canary failures caused by wrong digest on mutable tag due to CI race and cache/lock issue. No major customer impact; small 5xx uptick mitigated by disabling canary traffic and pinning correct digest.

incident-bot: please include these as immediate postmortem actions: kill-switch used, rollout paused, digest pinned, registry tag protected, and pipeline fix PR filed.

ashley: oncall handoff — I need to step out in 25m. @jon can you take over the rest of follow-ups?

jon: I’ll take it. I’ll stay on slack and drive the pipeline patch and add tests.

maya: thanks team. Logging follow-up action items in #incidents and will convert to a postmortem doc template. Also tagging customers with potential exposure list for outreach if retro shows widening impact.

leo: one-liner for change log: "Fix: ensure CI tagging is atomic, replace mutable `prod-canary` tag with immutable digest referencing; add registry protection and concurrent-run tests."

ops-oncall: closing the active page. monitoring for 30m.

incident-bot: Incident S2 downgraded to S3 and set to monitoring after mitigations.

maya: last note — action owners: ashley (registry tag policy + hotfix), leo (pipeline refactor), jon (tests + follow-up), maya (postmortem + customer assessment).

jon: copy. I’ll send a short summary to #product and #support after we finalize the postmortem draft.

maya: thumbs: :thumbsup:.
